stories.title: 2 soldiers martyred, 14 terrorists killed in North Waziristan operations: ISPR
summary: The statement said that sanitisation operations would continue to eliminate “remaining holed up khwarij from these areas”, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country.
The operations come a day after ISPR said 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.
On Friday, it said 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted over 48 hours in KP, including 35 in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, and eight in Orakzai district.

stories.title: KP Governor Kundi announces suspension of gold mining across province
summary: Addressing a press conference in Peshawar, Governor Kundi condemned the attack in Kohat that claimed the lives of 10 police personnel returning from an operation against illegal mining in the region.
On the Kohat incident, Governor Kundi said that following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule, the administration had launched an operation against illegal gold mining.

The miners used to pay extortion money to the terrorists and, in return, received protection from them,” the governor said, adding that this nexus was responsible for the martyrdom of the police personnel.

stories.title: ‘A moral red line’? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution
summary: Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy.
The United States refers to an “appropriate level of human judgement” in the use of autonomous weapons.

The autonomous weapons to be discussed in Geneva are not yet in widespread use, although analysts have noted that they have been deployed by Russia in its invasion of Ukraine as well as US attacks in Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16
summary: The meeting will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies, the FO said in a statement.

The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said.
During the summit, Pakistan called for enhanced intra-regional trade, transport connectivity, energy cooperation and sustainable development, while reaffirming its commitment to the ECO Vision 2025.

stories.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
summary: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.
Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.
Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but will not be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

stories.title: US air travel resumption will 'take time' after hours-long stop
summary: Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time.

We’re kind of stuck.” Travelers were left in the dark on the groundstop, with some saying they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could.

Susan Sardina said she had boarded her flight back to Orange County, California when staff told passengers there was a problem. “We were already on our flight to leave and we were told to get off,” she told AFP as she stood in a lengthy queue for a rental car.

stories.title: Police foil attack on checkpost in KP's Bannu, eliminate four terrorists
summary: BANNU: Police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu district on Friday night, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation, a police spokesperson said.

According to the police spokesperson, heavily armed terrorists launched a sudden attack on the checkpost last night. “However, police personnel deployed at the checkpost responded promptly and successfully repelled the assault,” he stated.

The spokesperson said that police also seized four Kalashnikov rifles, several magazines, a substantial quantity of ammunition, hand grenades and bandoliers, adding that the identification of the slain terrorists was underway.

stories.title: Wasim Akram questions Cummins’ Sandpapergate denial, says bowlers would spot tampering

The Australia captain maintained that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field and denied being an architect of the ball-tampering scheme.

stories.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
summary: AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

stories.title: Stench of ‘Sandpapergate’ set to linger as scandal reignites
summary: Australian captain Pat Cummins wants to draw a line under “Sandpapergate” and move on, but the stench of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is set to linger after a week of sensational accusations and denials.

Cummins repeated multiple times that he was not aware of the plan, insisting Khawaja’s version of events was “100 per cent wrong”. “I don’t want to talk about this again after today… because at some point we’ve got to move on,” he added.
That prompted Warner to blast Cummins for throwing Khawaja “under the bus” and The Australian newspaper to declare that “a generation of Australian players is officially at war”.

stories.title: ‘I may lose my mind’: Frustrated travelers stuck in US flight havoc
summary: In New York’s busy LaGuardia airport, Janice Llewellyn was on the verge of tears: the chaos could mean she will miss her daughter’s wedding in Toronto.
I wish they had another flight, I wish I could get another flight, like, now.” Planes wait at the terminal of LaGuardia Airport, New York on November 13, 2026.

stories.title: Labourer dies during underpass construction in KP
summary: The rescue authorities received a call that two labourers were trapped under the soil, according to a statement issued by the rescue service.
It said two ambulances were dispatched to the site soon after receiving the call, adding that the teams immediately began relief operations and safely recovered one trapped labourer alive.
However, the search continued, and the rescue personnel later recovered the body of a 28-year-old labourer, Naveed.

stories.title: Two suspects held for murdering minor boy in KP's Lakki
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Police arrested two suspects during a raid on Friday in connection with the murder of a two-year-old boy.

Speaking at a press conference here, District Police Officer (DPO) Sajjad Ahmad Sahibzada said that on Oct 28, Sifatullah, 27, reported to police that his son Sohail, 2, had gone missing while playing outside his house in the Wanda Shahabkhel area.

He said that there was some writing on the corpse, and all these elements helped track down the suspect. “The suspect’s home is located at a stone’s throw from the victim’s house, and that human intelligence was utilised to locate him,” he added.

stories.title: Policeman booked for allegedly aiding woman prisoner to escape in Islamabad
summary: The next day a three-members’ police team – a lady ASI, a lady constable and a constable/police driver - took the beggars, including the woman, to the court of assistant commissioner sub-divisional magistrate city for the hearing.
The court’s order and the beggars were handed over to the police driver, and the lady ASI left from the spot for the hearing of another case.

Investigations over the matter, including footages of the CCTVs installed there, revealed that the police driver, allegedly in collusion with the family of the woman, helped her escape from the parking of the district courts.

stories.title: Minor boy’s body recovered from Karachi's Lyari river

In the second incident, a motorcyclist, identified as Qasim Khan, 65, was killed when an unidentified vehicle hit him near the Sunday Bazaar in Ayub Goth, New Karachi.

stories.title: ‘Country’s first sponge park’ to save rainwater, cut urban flooding risk in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: A water sensitive sponge park, which was recently inaugurated in Gulberg Town, will help manage rainwater as it has the capacity to hold up to 100,000 gallons during the monsoon events, experts associated with World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-P) said on Friday.

The WWF-P in collaboration with the Gulberg Town Municipal Corporation and GSK (GlaxoSmithKline) has introduced a unique urban green space design at Jamali Park in Federal B Area, Block 8, to manage rainwater, enhance infiltration and reduce surface run-off.

It was officially inaugurated as Pakistan’s first water sensitive sponge park at a ceremony that brought together representatives from government, academia, civil society members, corporate partners and local residents.

stories.title: Balochistan Liberation Front terrorist jailed for 48 years in Chinese engineers’ attack case
summary: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court has sentenced a terrorist belonging to the banned Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) to a total of 48 years in prison for carrying out an attack on a car carrying two Chinese engineers near Gulbai Bridge in 2021.
He added that during the initial interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed his crime that in 2021, he along with co-accused Nasir Baloch had attacked the Chinese engineers.
The court noted that the attack on Chinese nationals, in the circumstances established in the present case, could not be treated merely as an ordinary offence of attempted murder.

stories.title: Rs2.5m recovered from ‘fake’ faith healer in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday claimed to have recovered Rs2.5 million from a woman posing as a faith healer, who allegedly defrauded women online by offering spiritual treatment for their problems.
The NCCIA said a woman fell victim to financial fraud through a Facebook page titled “Qurani Wazaif,” operated by a woman posing as a peerni.
She later realised that she had been defrauded and approached the agency.= Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

stories.title: Conductor punished for pushing woman off bus in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A private transport company had to sack a conductor who pushed a woman off a bus when she was trying to board the vehicle at a terminal here on Friday, after a video of the episode went viral, grabbing the attention of the Punjab government.

Some passersby recorded video of the incident and shared it on social media, triggering public outrage and the government’s reaction.The video shows the woman was trying to board the bus when the conductor pushed her.
Taking notice of the incident, Punjab Minister for Transport and Mass Transit Bilal Akbar Khan said the conductor had been sacked by the transport company.

stories.title: Police get remand of PTI leader Mian Usman Akram in May 9 case
summary: The investigating officer asked the court to allow shifting of Akram to jail to conduct an identification parade.
Earlier, the Lahore High Court disposed of a petition challenging Akram’s detention after the Punjab government withdrew his detention order.
A law officer informed the court that the notification regarding Akram’s detention had been withdrawn.

stories.title: Yemen's government-aligned forces repel Houthi attack as fighting has displaced over 340,000 people
summary: Yemen's government-aligned forces said Saturday that they had repelled a Houthi attack in the southwestern province of Lahj, while state-run media reported airstrikes targeting Houthi reinforcements in the neighbouring Taiz province.

Government forces control the city of Taiz and other parts of the province, while the Houthis have advanced in recent weeks in rural and coastal areas of Al-Mokha, Al-Shamayatayn, Al-Ma’afer, Jabal Habashi and Al-Wazi’iyah, according to an Anadolu correspondent.
Fighting between government forces and the Houthis has intensified since July, particularly in the Taiz province, which overlooks the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly speaker endorses referendum proposal on new provinces
summary: LAHORE: Endorsing a proposal to hold a referendum on the creation of new provinces in the country, Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan says the will of the masses holds supremacy over the opinion of elected representatives on matters of public importance.

Speaking to a private television channel, Rana Sana pointed out that the question of who holds the authority to conduct such a referendum remained unresolved, adding that any constitutional process regarding the carving out of new units would have to go through the parliament.
During his media talk in Lahore, Speaker Khan also touched upon broader political and governance issues.

stories.title: Microsoft restores service to Outlook and Teams after global outage
summary: Microsoft said on Saturday that services had fully recovered across Teams, Outlook and its other products, ending a global outage that crippled online communications for businesses and governments for over 24 hours.

Another outage for Microsoft The outage, reports of which started climbing around 1725 GMT on Thursday according to Ookla, is one of the longest in Microsoft's history and the second disruption to its services this year.
Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online — its cloud-based email and scheduling hub — leaving unconnected applications operational.

stories.title: Snowfall strands passengers, cargo at Khunjerab
summary: A GB police official told Dawn that snowfall was continuing at Khunjerab Top, leaving several vehicles and dozens of containers carrying imported goods from China stranded for hours.
In a press release, the GB police spokesperson said heavy snowfall was continuing from Dhee Headquarters to Khunjerab Top, while accumulated snow had made the road hazardous for travel.

In a video message, Minister Naiknaam Karim said snowfall had also occurred on the Chinese side, but the road had been cleared for traffic. “However, after entering the Pakistani side, we found the road at Khunjerab Top covered with approximately four inches of snow and ice.

stories.title: Fazl’s son skips another summons from NAB in Pakistan post case
summary: According to sources, the anti-graft watchdog will soon serve a third notice on the former minister and, in case he ignores it, NAB could take stern action, including his arrest.

Under the NAB notice, Asad Mehmood was req­uired to appear before the investigators to explain his position on alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure as federal minister.
Asad Mehmood had served as a federal minister during the Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) government in 2022-23.Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

stories.title: Balochistan Assembly seeks compulsory Arabic in primary schools
summary: The resolution was moved by JUI-F MPA Shahida Rauf, who said teaching basic Arabic would help students understand commonly used Quranic words and their meanings, enabling them to develop a better understanding of the Holy Quran from an early age.
The resolution called for a simple, standardised and grade-wise curriculum covering basic Arabic vocabulary, grammar and commonly used Quranic expressions.
Following the discussion, the Assembly unanimously approved the resolution, recommending the introduction of compulsory basic Arabic education in government primary schools throughout Balochistan.

stories.title: Act now on El Nino or pay double later, UNDP chief warns
summary: This exceptionally strong cycle has already battered economies worldwide. “Not acting is the most expensive climate policy that you could have,” De Croo warned, urging major players such as the International Monetary Fund to help vulnerable developing nations mitigate the damage.

Developing countries want more financial support from wealthier nations historically responsible for global warming, though De Croo acknowledged rich governments face heavy debt burdens and war costs.

While De Croo pressed for immediate adaptation investments and policy reforms to lower capital costs across 47 partner nations, questions over long-term global climate leadership also surfaced on the sidelines of the Antalya summit.

stories.title: COP31 must deliver climate justice, not empty pledges, says Sherry

The question is not whether the world has the resources, but whether it has the political will to redirect them,” Senator Rehman said.

stories.title: New provinces not anyone's wish but Pakistan's need: Mustafa Kamal
summary: Earlier this month, Kamal had reiterated his support for the creation of new provinces, saying Pakistan couldn't be governed under the existing administrative model and that the creation of new administrative units had become inevitable.
The minister had stated that Pakistan had a population of 260 million but only four provinces and argued that the creation of new administrative units had become necessary.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.

stories.title: Four terrorists killed as Bannu police foil attack on Kingar Pul checkpoint

stories.title: Yemeni govt forces fortify defences in Aden
summary: ABU DHABI: Yemen’s internationally recognised government is fortifying positions on the outskirts of Aden province, home to their de facto capital, as their Houthi foes seize hilltops overlooking the area, military officials told AFP.
The Houthis are now advancing east, consolidating their gains near the Red Sea while also moving closer to the Gulf of Aden.

The third military sou­rce, a field officer on the ground, said the Hou­this were advancing east of the strait towards the Gulf of Aden coast after taking large parts of Al-Madaribah wal Ara district.

stories.title: UN warns of rising maritime attacks, urges restoration of safe navigation in Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea
summary: A UN official warned on Friday that growing tensions and attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab threaten international peace and security, regional stability and the global economy.
Albudaiwi said the GCC reaffirms that attacks on member countries violate international law, threaten international peace and security, and require Council action.

"In conclusion, I wish to affirm that the GCC states are an active and reliable partner in supporting regional and international security and stability, and a fundamental pillar of the global economy and energy security," he said.

stories.title: Tanker collides with cruise ship in New Orleans, 32 hospitalised
summary: A tanker ship collided with a luxury paddle wheeler docked in New Orleans on the Mississippi River on Friday, causing the cruise vessel to roll over and sink as passengers scurried to disembark and dozens were flung into the water.
The accident occurred about midday when the tanker ship, the Atlantic Asphalt, "lost control and collided" with the docked cruise vessel, Moreno said.

Our hearts are with the passengers, crew, and families affected by this afternoon’s collision between a passenger vessel and a tanker on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, near the Crescent City Connection.

stories.title: Trump official seeks $50 billion for air traffic control after outage
summary: The Trump administration boosted its request for air traffic control funding to $50 billion late Friday after a communications issue forced a nationwide groundstop that halted thousands of flights for hours.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and the White House earlier on Friday asked for $30.1 billion to upgrade the United States' aging airports and air traffic control system.

The $30.1 billion request also includes $2 billion to replace and improve Federal Aviation Administration air traffic control towers and $18 billion for airport-related projects including $10 billion to modernise or replace aging terminals.

stories.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16
summary: The 30th Meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Foreign Ministers will be held in Islamabad on November 15-16, with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar set to chair the meeting, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said on Saturday.
According to the ministry, foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states would attend the meeting, along with representatives of the ECO Secretariat and its subsidiary bodies.

These efforts, it said, would contribute towards unlocking the region’s economic potential and ensuring that the benefits of regional cooperation translated into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states.

stories.title: Pakistan urges end to attacks on Gulf states, calls for regional de-escalation
summary: Pakistan has called for an end to military provocations and attacks in the Gulf region, urging the protection of civilians and commercial shipping and the pursuit of diplomatic solutions amid heightened regional tensions.

Addressing a United Nations Security Council meeting on the situation in the Gulf on Friday, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, said threats to maritime navigation and heightened tensions in the region were a matter of serious concern.

He said Pakistan would continue working with its brotherly and friendly countries and international partners to promote de-escalation, maritime security and lasting peace and stability in the region and beyond.

stories.title: Oil tanker hit by mine in Strait of Hormuz: Iranian media

stories.title: 13 ‘illegal’ Afghan nationals rounded up in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police continued search operations and a crackdown against illegal Afghan nationals residing in Rawalpindi, rounding up 13 persons, including eight women, and shifting them to the repatriation camp in H-9 for further legal proceedings.
The Rawalpindi district police and Special Branch are continuing the crackdown against illegal Afghan nationals residing in the district.

Earlier in October, the Punjab government had sought a report from the district police chiefs of six districts, including Rawalpindi, regarding the implementation of the illegal foreigners’ repatriation plan in line with the federal government’s policy.

stories.title: Two women killed in hit-and-run on Murree Road
summary: RAWALPINDI: Two working women were killed in a hit-and-run accident near Rehmanabad on Murree Road in the early hours of Friday, police said, adding that the car involved in the accident had been impounded while efforts were underway to arrest the driver.
The police said that the car involved in the accident had been impounded while efforts were underway to arrest the driver.
Meanwhile, a police official performing security duty during a cricket match at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium died after suffering a heart attack.
